## Proof

Let $k$ be a field with $\operatorname{char} k \neq 2$, and let $\mathbb{G}_m = \operatorname{Spec} k[t,t^{-1}]$ be the multiplicative group scheme over $k$. The subgroup $\{\pm 1\} = \mu_2 = \{x \in \mathbb{G}_m : x^2 = 1\}$ is the closed subgroup scheme cut out by $t^2 - 1 = 0$, which (since $\operatorname{char} k \neq 2$) is the reduced constant subgroup $\{1, -1\} \cong \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$.

**The map.** Define
$$\varphi : \mathbb{G}_m \longrightarrow \mathbb{G}_m, \qquad x \longmapsto x^2.$$
This is a homomorphism of algebraic groups: $(xy)^2 = x^2 y^2$. On coordinate rings it is the $k$-algebra homomorphism
$$\varphi^* : k[t, t^{-1}] \longrightarrow k[t, t^{-1}], \qquad t \longmapsto t^2.$$

**Kernel.** A point $x \in \mathbb{G}_m(R)$ (for a $k$-algebra $R$) lies in $\ker \varphi$ iff $x^2 = 1$, i.e. $x \in \mu_2(R)$. Hence
$$\ker \varphi = \mu_2 = \{\pm 1\}.$$

**Surjectivity (fppf epimorphism).** Via $\varphi^*$, the target ring $k[t,t^{-1}]$ becomes a module over the source ring $k[t,t^{-1}]$ (with $t$ acting as $t^2$). As such it is **free of rank 2** with basis $\{1, t\}$:
$$k[t, t^{-1}] = k[t^2, t^{-2}] \cdot 1 \;\oplus\; k[t^2, t^{-2}] \cdot t.$$
Indeed every Laurent polynomial $\sum a_n t^n$ splits into even and odd parts $\sum a_{2m} t^{2m} + t \sum a_{2m+1} t^{2m}$, both lying in $k[t^2, t^{-2}]$. Thus $\varphi^*$ is finite and flat, hence an **fppf covering**, so $\varphi$ is an epimorphism of fppf sheaves.

**The induced isomorphism.** Since $\varphi$ is an fppf epimorphism of group schemes with kernel $\mu_2$, the first isomorphism theorem for algebraic groups (in the fppf topology) gives an isomorphism
$$\bar\varphi : \mathbb{G}_m / \mu_2 \xrightarrow{\;\sim\;} \mathbb{G}_m$$
characterized by $\bar\varphi([x]) = x^2$, where $[x]$ is the class of $x$ in the quotient.

**Explicit description on coordinate rings.** The quotient $\mathbb{G}_m / \mu_2$ has coordinate ring the $\mu_2$-invariants:
$$k[\mathbb{G}_m/\mu_2] = k[t, t^{-1}]^{\mu_2}.$$
The generator $\sigma$ of $\mu_2$ acts by $t \mapsto -t$, so the invariants are precisely the even Laurent polynomials:
$$k[t, t^{-1}]^{\mu_2} = k[t^2, t^{-2}] \cong k[u, u^{-1}], \qquad u = t^2.$$
The isomorphism $\bar\varphi^* : k[u, u^{-1}] \to k[t^2, t^{-2}]$ sends $u \mapsto t^2$, which is an isomorphism of Hopf algebras (comultiplication $u \mapsto u \otimes u$ corresponds to $t^2 \mapsto t^2 \otimes t^2$).

**Conclusion.** The squaring map provides the explicit isomorphism
$$\boxed{\mathbb{G}_m / \{\pm 1\} \xrightarrow{\;\sim\;} \mathbb{G}_m, \qquad [x] \longmapsto x^2,}$$
with inverse (on the level of fppf sheaves) sending $y$ to the class of any square root of $y$. On coordinate rings it is the identification $k[u, u^{-1}] \xrightarrow{\sim} k[t, t^{-1}]^{\mu_2}$, $u \mapsto t^2$.
